places.name: Itanagar
places.summary: Arunachal's capital in the Himalayan foothills — Ita Fort, the state museum and forest-ringed Ganga Lake.
places.seoDescription: Itanagar: Ita Fort, the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum and Ganga Lake. Best October–April; by train to Naharlagun or fly to Tezpur.

images.alt: A forest-ringed lake in the hills around Itanagar
images.caption: Itanagar

overview.text:
Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh, spread across the green Himalayan foothills. It takes its name from Ita Fort, the 15th-century brick fort at its heart, which also gives the best view over the city.

Spend a morning at the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum, whose collection of textiles, handicrafts and archaeological finds is a good introduction to the state's cultures. Then head out to Ganga Lake, or Gyakar Sinyi, in old forest on the edge of town, for a boat ride or a walk around the shore. The food leans on bamboo shoots, fish and greens, with thukpa and momos everywhere. Come between October and April.

how_to_reach.text: Take a direct train to Naharlagun station, a few kilometres from the city, or fly to Tezpur in Assam and drive.

best_time.text: October to April is best, when the weather is pleasant for walks and sightseeing.

items.body: Climb Ita Fort for views over the city.
See the tribal collections at the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum.
Take a boat out on Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi).
Dishes built on bamboo shoots, fish and green vegetables.

places.name: Pasighat
places.summary: One of Arunachal's oldest towns, on the Siang — hanging bridges, Adi history and river dolphins at Daying Ering.
places.seoTitle: Pasighat — gateway to Arunachal on the Siang
places.seoDescription: Pasighat on the Siang: Kekar Monying hanging bridge, Daying Ering Wildlife Sanctuary's dolphins, Adi history. Best October–April.

images.alt: The bridge at Pasighat with green hills beyond
images.caption: Pasighat

overview.text:
Pasighat, headquarters of East Siang district, is one of the oldest towns in Arunachal Pradesh and is often called the gateway to the state. It sits low, at about 155 m, on the banks of the great Siang river.

The river shapes everything here. Kekar Monying, a traditional hanging bridge of bamboo and cane, swings over the Siang; the Kekar Monying rocks near Rottung were the site of a major Adi resistance against British forces in 1911. Across the water, Daying Ering Wildlife Sanctuary covers a wide floodplain where you can look for Gangetic dolphins and the Bengal florican by boat. Come between October and April. Dibrugarh airport is about 150 km away.

how_to_reach.text: Fly or take the train to Dibrugarh in Assam, about 150 km away, and continue by road.

items.body: Cross Kekar Monying, the bamboo-and-cane hanging bridge over the Siang.
Take a boat into Daying Ering Wildlife Sanctuary to look for river dolphins.
Learn the story of the Adi resistance of 1911.

best_time.text: October to April, when the weather suits sightseeing, wildlife trips and the river.

places.name: Roing
places.summary: A quiet valley town on the Dibang — base for Mayudia Pass, Mehao Lake and the ruins of Bhismaknagar.
places.seoTitle: Roing — Mayudia Pass, Mehao Lake and the Dibang valley
places.seoDescription: Roing on the Dibang river: Mayudia Pass (56 km), Mehao Lake (17 km), Sally Lake and Bhismaknagar Fort. Best October–April.

images.alt: Forested mountain ridges at Mayudia Pass
images.caption: Mayudia Pass, near Roing

overview.text:
Roing is a small town in the Lower Dibang Valley, set beside the braided channels of the Dibang river with forested hills rising all around. It is a base for some of the quietest corners of eastern Arunachal.

The road climbs about 56 km to Mayudia Pass, at nearly 8,000 ft, for wide mountain views. Mehao Lake and its wildlife sanctuary are about 17 km away, and Sally Lake, ringed by green forest, is just 3 km from town. For history and legend, Bhismaknagar Fort, about 30 km away, dates to around the 12th century and is said to have been the capital of King Bhismaka, father of Rukmini. Come between October and April; Dibrugarh airport is about 140–150 km away.

how_to_reach.text: Fly to Dibrugarh, about 140–150 km away, or take the train to Dibrugarh or Tinsukia, and continue by road.

items.body: Drive up to Mayudia Pass for mountain views.
Trek to Mehao Lake in its wildlife sanctuary.
Walk round Sally Lake, 3 km from town.
Visit the ruins of Bhismaknagar Fort.

best_time.text: October to April, when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing and outdoor trips.

places.name: Ita Fort
places.summary: The medieval brick fort that gave Itanagar its name — ramparts, gates and views over the capital.
places.seoDescription: Ita Fort, Itanagar: a 14th–15th-century brick fort of 80 lakh bricks with ramparts and gates. Open 8 am–4 pm.

images.alt: Brick ruins of Ita Fort on a grassy hilltop
images.caption: Ita Fort

overview.text:
Ita Fort — "ita" means brick — is the fort that gave Itanagar its name. It is usually dated to the 14th or 15th century; tradition credits King Ramachandra of the Jitari dynasty, between 1350 and 1450, though some historians argue for 1688.

What survives is the scale of it. The builders used some 80 lakh bricks and 45,000 man-days of labour. The eastern rampart runs for over half a kilometre with a single gate, the western for more than 1.4 km with two gates, and steep natural ridges complete the defences. Walk the walls between the gates and look out over the capital and the hills. It is open from 8 am to 4 pm.

places.name: Nuranang (Jang) Falls
places.summary: A 100 m waterfall by the road near Jang, between Sela and Tawang, named after the Monpa heroine Nura.
places.seoDescription: Nuranang, or Jang, Falls: a 100 m waterfall 2 km from Jang on the Tawang road, named after Nura, heroine of 1962. About 40 km from Tawang.

images.alt: Nuranang Falls pouring into a green gorge
images.caption: Nuranang Falls

overview.text:
Nuranang Falls — also called Jang Falls, or Bong Bong locally — drops about 100 metres down a forested cliff 2 km north-east of Jang town, on the motorable Jang Falls road. It lies on the NH-13 between Bomdila and Tawang, just north of the Sela Tunnel, so it is an easy stop on the drive up.

The falls carry a story from the 1962 war. They are named after Nura, a Monpa girl who helped Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat hold off the advancing army — the same story told at the Jaswant Garh memorial nearby. Walk down towards the foot of the falls to feel the spray. Tawang Monastery is about 40 km further on.

places.name: Bumla Pass
places.summary: A 15,000 ft border pass 37 km from Tawang — special permits, army posts and snow peaks.
places.seoTitle: Bumla Pass, Tawang — permits and what to expect
places.seoDescription: Bumla Pass: 4,572 m on the India–China border, 37 km from Tawang. Special permits through registered Tawang operators; Sangestar Tso nearby.

images.commons: File:Mountain range near Bum La Pass, Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh, India.jpg
images.alt: Snowy peaks and a mountain road near Bumla Pass
images.caption: Near Bumla Pass

overview.text:
Bumla Pass lies at 4,572 m (15,000 ft) on the India–China border, about 37 km from Tawang, and is one of the most dramatic places you can visit in Arunachal Pradesh. It was a key location in the 1962 war and remains a working border post near the Line of Actual Control.

Because the area is sensitive, you need a special permit, and trips are normally arranged through registered tour operators in Tawang. At the top, Indian Army personnel posted there often talk to visitors about life at this altitude. The road passes snowfields and high lakes; Sangestar Tso, also called Madhuri Lake, is nearby. Take warm layers and go slowly at this height.

items.title: Permit
items.body: Special permit via registered Tawang operators

places.name: Giant Buddha Statue, Tawang
places.summary: A 30 ft gilded-bronze Buddha on a hill above Tawang, near the monastery; open 6:30 am–7:30 pm.
places.seoDescription: Tawang's Giant Buddha: a 30 ft gilded-bronze statue near Tawang Monastery, with mountain views. Open 6:30 am–7:30 pm.

images.commons: File:The Giant Buddha Statue of Tawang.jpg
images.alt: The gilded Giant Buddha statue on its painted base
images.caption: Giant Buddha, Tawang

overview.text:
The Giant Buddha stands on a small hill near Tawang Monastery, a gilded-bronze figure almost 30 feet tall seated on a colourful painted base. It is a recent landmark, but it has quickly become one of the sights of Tawang.

The Buddha is shown in meditation, his right hand reaching down to touch the earth — the gesture of the moment of enlightenment. Walk around the base, then turn to the view: the hill looks out over the town and the mountains around it. The site is open from 6:30 am to 7:30 pm. Combine it with Tawang Monastery, a few kilometres away, and the Tawang War Memorial on the same circuit.

places.name: Urgelling Monastery
places.summary: A small 1487 gompa 3 km from Tawang, said to be the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama.
places.seoDescription: Urgelling Monastery, 3 km from Tawang: built in 1487, said to be the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama. Open 6 am–6 pm.

overview.text: Urgelling is a small gompa just 3 km from Tawang town, built in 1487 by Lama Urgen Sangpo. Legend says Tsangyang Gyatso, the 6th Dalai Lama, was born and grew up here. It is open from 6 am to 6 pm.

places.name: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary
places.summary: One of the world's top birding sites — 500+ species in 217 sq km, home of the Bugun liocichla.
places.seoTitle: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary — birding in Arunachal
places.seoDescription: Eaglenest, West Kameng: 500+ bird species, the Bugun liocichla, 500–3,250 m of forest. Best March–April; via Tezpur and Bhalukpong.

images.alt: A chestnut-tailed minla perched in Eaglenest
images.caption: Chestnut-tailed minla, Eaglenest

overview.text:
Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary covers 217 sq km of forest in West Kameng district and is rated among the best birding destinations in the world. More than 500 bird species have been recorded here, and the list is still growing; the sanctuary became famous in 2006 with the discovery of a new bird, the Bugun liocichla.

Its range is huge: the sanctuary climbs from 500 m to 3,250 m, so its forests change with height. Over 160 species of butterfly add to the colour. March and April are the best months for birds. Walk the trails with local guides, many from the communities who help protect the forest. Fly to Tezpur, about 120 km away, then drive 5–6 hours via Bhalukpong.

places.name: Pakke Tiger Reserve
places.summary: Arunachal's hornbill country — 862 sq km of forest with tigers, clouded leopards and an award-winning nest-adoption scheme.
places.seoTitle: Pakke Tiger Reserve — hornbills and tigers
places.seoDescription: Pakke (Pakhui) Tiger Reserve: 862 sq km, tigers and clouded leopards, 296+ birds and the award-winning Hornbill Nest Adoption Programme. Best November–March.

images.commons: File:Close wing position of Delias pasithoe Linnaeus, 1767 – Red-base Jezebel Butterflies of Pakke - 12.jpg
images.alt: A red-base Jezebel butterfly at Pakke
images.caption: Butterfly of Pakke

overview.text:
Pakke Tiger Reserve, also called Pakhui, spreads over 862 sq km of forest in the Pakke Kessang district and is one of the richest wildlife areas in Northeast India. It is best known for hornbills: its Hornbill Nest Adoption Programme, which protects endangered hornbills, won the India Biodiversity Award in 2016.

More than 40 species of mammal live here, among them the Bengal tiger, the Indian leopard and the clouded leopard, along with elephants, gaur and sambar. Over 296 bird species have been recorded, and the forests are alive with butterflies. The terrain climbs from 100 m to 2,000 m. Come between November and March, when the weather is pleasant and sightings are better. Tezpur is about 64 km away.

places.name: Lake of No Return
places.summary: A Second World War relic near Pangsau Pass on the Myanmar border, named for Allied aircraft lost there.
places.seoDescription: The Lake of No Return near Pangsau Pass: a WWII relic on the Stilwell Road. Best October–April.

overview.text: The Lake of No Return lies near Pangsau Pass on the India–Myanmar border in Changlang district, beside the wartime Stilwell (Ledo) Road. It is named for the Allied aircraft that reportedly crashed here flying supply routes over the Patkai hills in the Second World War. Go between October and April.

places.name: Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary
places.summary: A 337 sq km sanctuary of silver fir forest 30 km from Ziro.
places.seoDescription: Talley Valley, 30–32 km from Ziro: a 337 sq km sanctuary of fir forest, 1,200–3,000 m. Best October–April.

overview.text: Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary lies about 30–32 km north-east of Ziro. Set up in 1995, it covers some 337 sq km and climbs from 1,200 to 3,000 m, opening at around 2,400 m onto a plateau of silver fir. Visit between October and April.

places.name: Samten Yongcha Monastery
places.summary: Mechuka's 400-year-old hilltop monastery, looking over the Siyom valley; open 7 am–5 pm.
places.seoDescription: Samten Yongcha, Mechuka: a 400-year-old monastery on a hill above the Siyom valley. Open 7 am–5 pm.

images.alt: The Buddha and painted deities inside Mechuka's old monastery
images.caption: Samten Yongcha Monastery

overview.text:
Samten Yongcha Monastery has stood on its hill above the Mechuka valley for some 400 years, making it the spiritual heart of this remote town at 6,000 ft. From the gompa you look down over the wide valley and the Siyom river — known locally as Yargyap Chu — with snow peaks beyond.

Inside, old statues and painted images of the Buddha and of Guru Padmasambhava, founder of the Nyingma tradition, are the work of centuries of devotion. Prayer flags snap in the wind outside. The monastery is open from 7 am to 5 pm. Round off the day at Gurudwara Guru Nanak Taposthan, built in the 1980s by soldiers of the Sikh regiment, or the 200 ft Siko Dido falls on the road in.

places.name: Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary
places.summary: Forest and a clear 4 sq km lake 17 km from Roing, reached on a 12 km trek — red pandas and hoolock gibbons.
places.seoTitle: Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary and Mehao Lake
places.seoDescription: Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary near Roing: a 12 km trek to Mehao Lake, red pandas, hoolock gibbons and 200+ birds. Best October–March.

images.alt: Mehao Lake ringed by forested hills
images.caption: Mehao Lake

overview.text:
Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary lies about 17 km from Roing in the Lower Dibang Valley. Set up in 1980, it protects thick forest and some of the region's rarest animals, including the red panda and the hoolock gibbon, India's only ape.

At its heart is Mehao Lake, nearly 4 sq km of clear, still water ringed by forested hills. The way in is on foot: a 12 km trail that takes 4 to 7 hours. Around 60 species of mammal and more than 200 of birds live here, from clouded leopards to rufous-necked hornbills. There is no accommodation inside the sanctuary, so plan a long day from Roing. Go between October and March.
